newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Peking Apparel to seek listing in March - sources.
newsitem.headline: Peking Apparel to seek listing in March - sources.

text.p: Hong Kong-based leather garments manufacturer and distributor Peking Apparel International Group Ltd is expected to seek a listing in Hong Kong in early March, market sources said on Wednesday.
"As the company is still awaiting listing approval from the stock exchange, it gave very little detail on the offering," one analyst said after attending a company presentation.
"I think the issue size is likely to be a small one of about HK$50-HK$60 million."
Citicorp International Ltd is expected to be the sponsor of the issue, sources said.
Peking Apparel -- which has plants in China's southern Shenzhen economic zone -- designs, makes and distributes leather garments, they said.
In the fiscal year ended in March 1996, the Chinese market accounted for about 54 percent of the company's turnover, the U.S. market 31 percent and the Hong Kong market 5.8 percent, they said.
The company posted a turnover of HK$290.9 million for the year ended in March 1996, up from HK$224.7 million in 1995 and HK$166.8 million in 1994, sources said.
Net profit was HK$27.9 million in 1996, up from HK$19.6 million in 1995 and HK$24.1 million in 1994.
Turnover was HK$90.5 million for the five months to August 31, 1996, with net profit of HK$9.3 million, they said.
